search.snippet_policy: Native query radius10 produces matched excerpts; raw SQL adapter returns content[:200] and turn identifiers.

semantic_comparison.scope: No timing conclusion; same maintained seed closures, fresh native/SQLite authorities. Native full turn metadata and different search ranking/snippets make raw output semantics non-identical.

output_cost_control.scope: Exact captured output decode versus direct packed JSON snapshot SQL control. Packed document schema is not the production turn authority and not a full engine parity result. No native engine timing measured in this probe.

archiveAcceptance.scope: process-wide accepted background commits while request profiling is enabled; not durable or per-owner coverage

authorityHolds.scope: process lifetime; completed instrumented background holds; wall time, not CPU; counters may advance during snapshot; phases are not additive

requestProfile.scope: process lifetime; completed sampled dispatches; wall time, not CPU time

hydration_profile.scope: Profiler every1; seed and read operations retained separately; observer perturbs. No default-off latency verdict.

source_findings.full_turn_size_check: turn.rs:list_values_until serializes each materialized public turn into a discarded temporary Vec for MAX_TURN_RESPONSE_BYTES enforcement.
source_findings.list_encoding: conversation_header.rs:list encodes each projected conversation once then joins the encoded rows. No repeated whole-list serialization found.
source_findings.legacy_conversion: turn.rs:legacy_message moves private projection and metadata fields; no full-tree clone found here.

limitations: Expanded search limit covers every seeded hit; differing ranking and snippet policies prevent equivalence of the original top20 query.
Equal hydration content/timestamps are not equality of full response schema.
Packed SQL JSON snapshot is a decoding control, not normalized SQLite turn-authority parity.
Observer-enabled timings cannot allocate the default-off latency budget. Independent spans are not disjoint.
Repeated temporary turn encoding is a candidate cost, not a measured cause or an admitted optimization.
No runtime change, deployment, original harness pass, provider/browser coverage or universal superiority credit.
